turn2.differences: The author's c1 bundles three of my step-1 conditions (issue identity, Priya's authorship, and the API-timeout topic) into one clause, but this is just a grouping choice - it doesn't drop or add any substantive requirement. c2 and c3 map directly to my conditions 4 and 5. ambiguity_effects.explain: In isolation a careful reader can't be sure which year is meant, but every comment in the dataset that is otherwise relevant falls in 2026, so this ambiguity has no effect on which record is selected here.

Read as 'the comment thread has been marked resolved' (matching Linear's resolvingUserId/resolvedAt fields), i-web-20 is a clean, unique match. Read as 'the issue's workflow status is resolved/Done', no issue in the dataset has a completed-type status, so that reading would yield zero matches. The two readings therefore produce different outcomes (one match vs. none), even though the comment-thread reading is favored by proximity ('that' most naturally attaches to 'a comment ... resolved').

turn2.naturalness_note: The phrasing is a bit dense (packing person, topic, exact date, and resolution status into one sentence), which reads more like a disambiguation puzzle than casual speech, but each element is plausible for someone trying to pin down one issue among several similar ones in a real workspace. Nothing in the wording is implausible for a real Linear user familiar with comment-resolving.
